faqs.q: How do I play?
faqs.a: Tap a bubble to split it, and tap the smallest size to pop it. Swipe to slice several at once, and drag off the hinge to snap it and fling nearby bubbles back. Keep large bubbles from crossing the hinge: each crossing costs a shield, and losing all three restarts the level. The smallest bubbles pop on the hinge at no cost.

faqs.q: Can two people play?
faqs.a: Yes. In two-player mode each player owns one side of the hinge on the same screen. A bubble you let cross charges you and lands on your rival. Take their last shield and you win; if every bubble is cleared first, the higher score wins.

faqs.q: Is Metaphases free?
faqs.a: Yes. It is free in any browser, with no sign-up and no account.

faqs.q: Are the grades financial advice?
faqs.a: No. Setup grades, Compass grades, Market Mood and Hype Check flags are rules-based information computed from historical prices, consensus estimates and financial statements. Metaphases never says buy, sell or hold and never sets a price target.

faqs.q: What do the moon phases mean?
faqs.a: They show when a report lands: a waxing moon before the opening bell, a full moon during market hours, a waning moon after the close, and a dashed outline when the time is not known yet.

faqs.q: How does Compass know what is inside my ETFs?
faqs.a: It keeps a weekly snapshot of the top 10 holdings and weights of 25 popular ETFs, multiplies your fund value by each company's weight, and adds any shares you hold directly.

faqs.q: Where is my data stored?
faqs.a: On your device, in your browser's local storage. There are no accounts, analytics, trackers or ads, and a personal AI key travels only with the request that uses it and is never stored on the server.

faqs.q: Where does the data come from?
faqs.a: Finnhub, FRED, Nasdaq and Yahoo Finance.

faqs.q: Is there a version for kids?
faqs.a: Yes. Metaphases has a separate kids area, and a companion iPhone and iPad app for kids called Moon Club. Its download goes through a grown-up page at https://mutaafaziz.com/metaphases/kids/app.

title: 17-0: Football Franchise Simulator
description: Spin a franchise and an era to fill seven slots. Use your skills to chase a perfect season in this history-inspired game.
summary: 17-0 (at 18-0.co) is a free pro football history game that runs in a web browser at 18-0.co. Each spin lands on a franchise and an era; you take exactly one player season from it, fill seven slots (a quarterback, two running backs, two receivers, a tight end and a team defense), and get a deterministic rating mapped to a 17-game record from 0-17 to 17-0. Every card is a real season from 1980 to 2025, rated against its own era, with 4,872 rated seasons across 218 franchise-era combinations built from nflverse data. The same roster always earns the same record, and ranked seasons are scored on the server. It is open source (MIT); a public TestFlight beta exists for iPhone and iPad, and no account is required to play.

faqs.q: Is 17-0 at 18-0.co free?
faqs.a: Yes. It is free to play in a web browser at 18-0.co, and no account is required.

faqs.q: How does a game work?
faqs.a: Spin for a franchise and an era, take exactly one player from it, and repeat until seven slots are filled: a quarterback, two running backs, two receivers, a tight end and a team defense. The roster is rated and mapped to a 17-game record.

faqs.q: How often does someone go 17-0?
faqs.a: Measured against the real dataset over 400,000 games, 17-0 lands about once in 6,000 games and 16-1 about once in 49.

faqs.q: Are the players and stats real?
faqs.a: Yes. Every card is a real regular season from 1980 to 2025, built from nflverse data and licensed season tables, and rated against its own era. Franchises are named for the city they play in now.

faqs.q: Is there an iPhone app?
faqs.a: A public TestFlight beta for iPhone and iPad is linked from the project's README. On any device, the web version can be installed from the browser and plays offline.

faqs.q: Does 17-0 collect data or show ads?
faqs.a: No account is needed; signing in is optional so ranked seasons can follow you. The game uses PostHog product analytics, and the web build may show display ads on the results screen.
